overview: Samoan life connects aiga, language, genealogy and chiefly institutions through fa'asamoa. This card focuses on cultural continuity and the colonial-to-independent period represented by this imported record. It does not treat the modern state as identical to every earlier Samoan community.

items.text: Fa'asamoa links family, language, genealogies, matai and ceremonial obligations. Service, respect and love organise reciprocal relationships among generations.
Samoans exchanged news, goods and marriage partners with neighbouring Pacific peoples, including Tongans and Fijians. These connections long preceded colonial partition.
John Williams arrived with Christian teaching. Samoan communities subsequently developed forms of Christianity intertwined with fa'asamoa.
Diaspora communities sustain Samoan-language early education and school programmes. These institutions connect language learning with shared leadership and cultural knowledge.
Western Samoa regained independence following New Zealand administration. Samoan culture also continues in American Samoa and overseas communities; political borders do not contain the whole people.
